note: The closest fit to the stated ICP in this batch, and it fails on the same criterion as everyone else. Business owner running a six-figure construction and renovation company with multi-million ambitions — the archetype the ICP describes. Health has been crowded out by the business rather than being in crisis: 'I'm not giving me enough time for growth, mentally, nor physically... I'm just very occupied by productivity in the business.' He is emphatically not deconditioned at around 8% body fat with a six-pack after two years off, ex semi-pro athlete. And he answered the good-to-great question verbatim when asked: 'are you looking to get back into shape or are you looking to be your best?' / 'To be my best.' Income is the sole miss and it is unambiguous — credit card debt just cleared, roughly $700/month servicing truck and surgery debt, a $7,800 monthly break-even, a stated safe ceiling of $250/month, and a Klarna decline at a 758 credit score. He bought anyway, on 12-month financing. This is a third supporting data point for the existing observation that income screening filters out deals a payment plan carries, and the strongest one, because on every other criterion he is the customer the ICP was written to describe.
